Population-weighted centroids of larger units

Source: R/acc.R
acc_centroids.Rd

Places one point in each larger unit, such as a census tract, at the population-weighted mean location of its blocks. These points are the usual origins for access measures. A tract's geometric center can fall in empty land; its population-weighted centroid falls where people live.

Usage

acc_centroids(blocks, by, weight)

Arguments

blocks

An sf object of small units, usually census blocks, with point or polygon geometry. Each polygon is first replaced by a point inside it (sf::st_point_on_surface()). Passing points is faster: the 2020 TIGER/Line block files carry an internal point for each block (INTPTLON20, INTPTLAT20).

by

<tidy-select> One column naming the larger unit each block belongs to. For 2020 blocks the tract is the first 11 characters of the block GEOID.

weight

<tidy-select> One numeric column of non-negative block weights, usually total population.

Value

An sf object of points, one row per unit sorted by unit, with the by column, the summed weight column, n_blocks, and the CRS of blocks.

Details

The centroid of unit \(u\) is the weighted mean $$(\bar x_u, \bar y_u) = \frac{\sum_{b \in u} w_b (x_b, y_b)}{\sum_{b \in u} w_b}.$$ A unit whose blocks all have zero weight, such as a tract of parkland or water, gets the unweighted mean of its block points instead, and a message counts such units.

Means are taken in the coordinates of blocks, so project to a planar CRS first, such as California Albers (EPSG:3310). With longitude and latitude the mean is a planar approximation: close within a tract, poor across a large unit.

See also

acc_cost_matrix(), which takes these points as origins.

Examples

blocks <- sf::st_as_sf(
  data.frame(
    tract = c("t1", "t1", "t2"),
    pop = c(1, 3, 5),
    x = c(0, 4, 10),
    y = c(0, 0, 10)
  ),
  coords = c("x", "y"),
  crs = 3310
)
# t1 sits at (0 * 1 + 4 * 3) / 4 = 3 on the x axis.
acc_centroids(blocks, tract, pop)
#> Simple feature collection with 2 features and 3 fields
#> Geometry type: POINT
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 3 ymin: 0 xmax: 10 ymax: 10
#> Projected CRS: NAD83 / California Albers
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   tract   pop n_blocks    geometry
#> * <chr> <dbl>    <int> <POINT [m]>
#> 1 t1        4        2       (3 0)
#> 2 t2        5        1     (10 10)
